title: Dielectric loss in superconducting qubit materials
bottleneck: Superconducting qubits lose quantum coherence largely through two-level-system defects in amorphous dielectrics, interfaces, and surface oxides. Despite years of materials work, coherence times have plateaued: the microscopic identity of the dominant lossy defects is still debated, and no fabrication route reproducibly eliminates them. Each new qubit design re-encounters the same interface-loss wall.
why_it_blocks: Coherence time directly limits the depth of quantum circuits and the overhead of error correction. Materials-limited coherence means fault-tolerant quantum computing needs millions more physical qubits than a low-loss platform would, pushing timelines out by years.
current_state: State-of-the-art transmons reach a few hundred microseconds of coherence through cleaner interfaces and crystalline dielectrics, but gains are incremental. The 2026 SuperC materials-search pipeline may surface new low-loss superconductors, though qubit-specific materials screening is still in its infancy.
